## Problem

Completed changes have no shared changelog or established writing guideline, and the change harness does not require a changelog entry in the implementation PR. Readers need a concise account of what changed and why it matters.

## Required outcome

Create `CHANGELOG.md` with the already solved issues below, document the approved writing guideline separately, and make changelog maintenance part of the harness's implementation and review workflow. Add only a short instruction and guideline reference to `AGENTS.md`.

## Approved changelog guideline

> Write each changelog entry as one short, clear sentence stating what changed and the specific problem it fixes or benefit it provides. Prefix the entry with a topic tag, using the associated epic's name where applicable; omit the tag when no meaningful topic fits. Describe delivered behavior and avoid unsupported claims.

Suggested pattern: **[Topic] [Changed what] so [practical benefit].** Use plain language and name the affected behavior or component. Describe the delivered behavior rather than simply rephrasing the issue title, and keep the benefit within the change's actual scope. Topic tags are useful grouping, not mandatory invented categories; use concise epic-derived names such as **[Observability]** and **[Harness]**. Include a link to the associated issue for traceability.

## Initial entries reviewed with the user

- **[Observability]** Improved Vulkan and cache error logs to preserve error codes and affected resources so failures are easier to diagnose. ([#10](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/10))
- **[Observability]** Fixed list, rehash and prune commands to report failure when resource parsing fails so incomplete processing cannot appear successful. ([#11](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/11))
- **[Observability]** Fixed file write helpers to report write, flush and close errors so callers can detect incomplete output. ([#12](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/12))
- **[Harness]** Added a resumable change workflow with independent checks so interrupted implementation work can continue with its progress and review evidence preserved. ([#34](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/34))
- **[Harness]** Included verified backlog completion in implementation PRs so merged changes update task status without a separate follow-up. ([#35](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/35))
- **[Harness]** Added remote publication of change workflow records so plans, reports and recovery checkpoints remain available beyond the local checkout. ([#36](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/36))
- **[Harness]** Moved task tracking to GitHub Issues so contributors can find requirements, progress and blocking dependencies in one place. ([#37](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/37))
- **[Harness]** Added one-command delivery after explicit approval so merging, branch cleanup and task closeout can resume after interruptions. ([#39](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39))

These describe delivered changes, checked in this conversation against merged PRs #42, #44, #45, #2, #5, #6, #38 and #41 respectively. Entry #35 is historical behavior subsequently replaced by GitHub issue tracking in #37; preserve that distinction rather than presenting the old backlog mechanism as current behavior. Recheck completion and delivery evidence during implementation; closed-but-not-planned or incomplete work must not be represented as delivered.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Add root `CHANGELOG.md`, seeded with all eight reviewed entries and their issue links; use an understandable historical ordering/grouping without inventing release versions or release dates.
2. Store the full guideline in a dedicated tracked document, preferably `local-docs/changelog-guidelines.md`, and link it from the documentation index and changelog as appropriate. Include the approved sentence pattern, optional topic tags, accurate scope and issue traceability.
3. Update the tracked harness instructions so each implementation PR includes the relevant changelog entry alongside the change. Ensure implementers add or revise the entry and independent checkers verify its accuracy, topic, brevity and inclusion in the reviewed candidate; final review covers the changelog too. Follow any existing installed-skill synchronization policy where applicable.
4. Add a short `AGENTS.md` instruction requiring changelog updates with changes and linking to the dedicated guideline. Keep detailed writing rules and examples out of `AGENTS.md`.
5. Changelog wording follows the final delivered scope if implementation changes during review, and does not claim unsupported, failed or incomplete work as completed. Maintain GitHub Issues as task authority; the changelog is a historical change record, not a second backlog.

## Verification expectations

- Reconcile the eight initial entries with completed issue state and actual merged PR evidence; verify issue links and historical scope, especially #35 versus #37.
- Review Markdown rendering, links, topic consistency and the one-sentence change-and-benefit format.
- Check the harness instructions cover implementation, independent checking and final review, with `AGENTS.md` pointing to one authoritative guideline.
- Run applicable documentation/skill validation and whitespace checks under `local-docs/verification.md`; run meaningful harness regression checks if runtime behavior changes. Report actual checks and limitations without claiming product verification for documentation changes.

## Scope

Changelog creation and backfill, contributor guidance and harness instructions. This issue files the requested work; it does not implement it. No C++/Vulkan behavior changes or new release automation are requested. Related parent: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9.

<!-- fossilize-changelog-guideline-v1 -->

## Problem

Completed changes have no shared changelog or established writing guideline, and the change harness does not require a changelog entry in the implementation PR. Readers need a concise account of what changed and why it matters.

## Required outcome

Create `CHANGELOG.md` with the already solved issues below, document the approved writing guideline separately, and make changelog maintenance part of the harness's implementation and review workflow. Add only a short instruction and guideline reference to `AGENTS.md`.

## Approved changelog guideline

> Write each changelog entry as one short, clear sentence stating what changed and the specific problem it fixes or benefit it provides. Prefix the entry with a topic tag, using the associated epic's name where applicable; omit the tag when no meaningful topic fits. Describe delivered behavior and avoid unsupported claims.

Suggested pattern: **[Topic] [Changed what] so [practical benefit].** Use plain language and name the affected behavior or component. Describe the delivered behavior rather than simply rephrasing the issue title, and keep the benefit within the change's actual scope. Topic tags are useful grouping, not mandatory invented categories; use concise epic-derived names such as **[Observability]** and **[Harness]**. Include a link to the associated issue for traceability.

## Initial entries reviewed with the user

- **[Observability]** Improved Vulkan and cache error logs to preserve error codes and affected resources so failures are easier to diagnose. ([#10](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/10))
- **[Observability]** Fixed list, rehash and prune commands to report failure when resource parsing fails so incomplete processing cannot appear successful. ([#11](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/11))
- **[Observability]** Fixed file write helpers to report write, flush and close errors so callers can detect incomplete output. ([#12](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/12))
- **[Harness]** Added a resumable change workflow with independent checks so interrupted implementation work can continue with its progress and review evidence preserved. ([#34](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/34))
- **[Harness]** Included verified backlog completion in implementation PRs so merged changes update task status without a separate follow-up. ([#35](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/35))
- **[Harness]** Added remote publication of change workflow records so plans, reports and recovery checkpoints remain available beyond the local checkout. ([#36](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/36))
- **[Harness]** Moved task tracking to GitHub Issues so contributors can find requirements, progress and blocking dependencies in one place. ([#37](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/37))
- **[Harness]** Added one-command delivery after explicit approval so merging, branch cleanup and task closeout can resume after interruptions. ([#39](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/39))

These describe delivered changes, checked in this conversation against merged PRs #42, #44, #45, #2, #5, #6, #38 and #41 respectively. Entry #35 is historical behavior subsequently replaced by GitHub issue tracking in #37; preserve that distinction rather than presenting the old backlog mechanism as current behavior. Recheck completion and delivery evidence during implementation; closed-but-not-planned or incomplete work must not be represented as delivered.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Add root `CHANGELOG.md`, seeded with all eight reviewed entries and their issue links; use an understandable historical ordering/grouping without inventing release versions or release dates.
2. Store the full guideline in a dedicated tracked document, preferably `local-docs/changelog-guidelines.md`, and link it from the documentation index and changelog as appropriate. Include the approved sentence pattern, optional topic tags, accurate scope and issue traceability.
3. Update the tracked harness instructions so each implementation PR includes the relevant changelog entry alongside the change. Ensure implementers add or revise the entry and independent checkers verify its accuracy, topic, brevity and inclusion in the reviewed candidate; final review covers the changelog too. Follow any existing installed-skill synchronization policy where applicable.
4. Add a short `AGENTS.md` instruction requiring changelog updates with changes and linking to the dedicated guideline. Keep detailed writing rules and examples out of `AGENTS.md`.
5. Changelog wording follows the final delivered scope if implementation changes during review, and does not claim unsupported, failed or incomplete work as completed. Maintain GitHub Issues as task authority; the changelog is a historical change record, not a second backlog.

## Verification expectations

- Reconcile the eight initial entries with completed issue state and actual merged PR evidence; verify issue links and historical scope, especially #35 versus #37.
- Review Markdown rendering, links, topic consistency and the one-sentence change-and-benefit format.
- Check the harness instructions cover implementation, independent checking and final review, with `AGENTS.md` pointing to one authoritative guideline.
- Run applicable documentation/skill validation and whitespace checks under `local-docs/verification.md`; run meaningful harness regression checks if runtime behavior changes. Report actual checks and limitations without claiming product verification for documentation changes.

## Scope

Changelog creation and backfill, contributor guidance and harness instructions. This issue files the requested work; it does not implement it. No C++/Vulkan behavior changes or new release automation are requested. Related parent: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/9.
